title: ContextEnvelope
description: The bounded operating context handed to an agent (CAO). Agents consume ContextEnvelopes; they receive no raw vault access, no raw index access, and no ambient authority. A ContextEnvelope COMPOSES one or more RCA ContextBundles (docs/contracts/CONTEXT_BUNDLE.md) plus active scope, capabilities, denied scopes, policies, memory/mutation/execution rules, cross-scope flows, and escalation conditions. It does NOT replace ContextBundle. A ContextEnvelope is a projection, not primary evidence.

access_mode.description: Asserts the only access the consuming agent has is this bounded context. There is no field that grants raw vault or raw index access.

user_intent.description: The intent/task this envelope was assembled to serve.

allowed_capabilities.description: The capability grants the agent may exercise within this envelope. Empty means read/reason only.

denied_scopes.description: Scopes explicitly NOT available in this envelope. Required and may be empty. Denied scopes are recorded as denials with reasons, never passed as hidden context. Useful-but-denied material becomes an escalation condition, not silent inclusion.

cross_scope_flows.description: Typed CrossScopeFlow grants in effect for this envelope. Required and may be empty. Any cross-scope material present must be attributable to one of these flows; similarity is not permission.

retrieved_items.description: Individual context items available to the agent. Each item carries EXACTLY ONE metadata source — never both — so there is a single source of identity/provenance and no drift: either an embedded metadata bundle (identity is the bundle's object_id) OR a metadata-bundle reference paired with an explicit object_id. No naked content.

oneOf.$comment: Embedded bundle: the metadata bundle is the single source of identity and metadata; no separate object_id (it would drift from the bundle) and no reference.
Referenced bundle: object_id identifies the item and metadata_bundle_ref points to its bundle; the embedded bundle is absent. The two never coexist.

context_bundles.description: References to the RCA ContextBundles (docs/contracts/CONTEXT_BUNDLE.md) this envelope composes. The envelope references bundles; it does not redefine or replace them. Required and may be empty.

non_authority.description: Marks the composed bundle as candidate evidence/projection, never authority.

citation_policy.description: What the agent may cite and how. Retrieval/inclusion permission does NOT imply citation permission.

cross_scope_citation_requires_flow.description: Citing material across a scope boundary requires a typed CrossScopeFlow that allows `cite`.

memory_policy.description: What the agent may remember from this envelope. Remembering does not make material canonical.

remembered_authority_state.description: Anything remembered enters machine memory as noncanonical; promotion is a separate governed transition.

mutation_policy.description: Whether and how durable mutation may be proposed. Agents propose; they never mutate durable knowledge directly.

mutation_allowed.description: Whether the agent may PROPOSE a durable mutation. Even when true, it proposes; it does not write.

requires_authority_transition.description: Any durable mutation routes through a governed AuthorityTransition (authority-transition.schema.json). Persistence is not authority.

execution_policy.description: Whether and how side effects may be requested. Execution cannot authorize itself.

execution_allowed.description: Whether the agent may REQUEST execution. The request is authorized by GOV, then performed by EXE.

requires_authorization.description: Every side effect requires a prior governed authorization; the agent cannot self-authorize.

escalation_conditions.description: Conditions under which the agent must escalate to a human/governance instead of acting or silently dropping context. Required and may be empty. Useful denied material should surface here rather than be hidden.

denial_class.description: Category of the denial that motivated the escalation, when applicable; non-identifying.

audit_ref.description: Opaque reference to an audit-only record holding any related scope/object identifiers. Never the identifiers themselves — an escalation must not leak the existence of a denied scope.
